Hypothesis: We hypothesize that CIAO2A acts as a central integrator of mRNA export and epitranscriptomic regulation in liver cancer. By physically interacting with the export factors NXF1 and ALYREF, CIAO2A contributes to the formation of export-competent mRNP complexes. Concurrently, CIAO2A recruits and/or modulates the activity of RNA modification enzymes—responsible for marks such as m6A and pseudouridine—thereby generating a modification signature on tumor suppressor mRNAs. This signature, potentially defined by unique RNA sequence or structural motifs, confers high-fidelity and selective export of these transcripts to the cytoplasm. The resultant optimal expression of tumor suppressor and regulatory proteins serves to counteract oncogenic factors, exemplified by eIF5A2, and thereby suppress processes such as metastasis and angiogenesis. Impaired function of CIAO2A, conversely, is expected to diminish this selective export, promoting tumor progression. Our investigation will employ a suite of advanced technologies including CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing, the creation of domain-specific mutants, co-immunoprecipitation and proximity labeling to validate protein-protein interactions, single-molecule RNA FISH to trace transcript localization, and comprehensive multi-omics analyses to delineate transcriptomic and epitranscriptomic landscapes in liver cancer models.
Abstract: We propose that CIAO2A functions as an integrative dual-regulator in liver cancer by coordinating both the mRNA export machinery and the deposition of selective RNA modifications on tumor suppressor transcripts. Specifically, upregulation of CIAO2A recruits essential export factors (NXF1, ALYREF) and concurrently organizes local microdomains that facilitate the recruitment and activity of RNA modification enzymes (e.g., m6A and pseudouridine writers). In doing so, CIAO2A promotes the deposition of specific RNA marks on tumor suppressor mRNAs, potentially via recognition of unique RNA motifs, ensuring their selective, high-fidelity export and subsequent optimal protein translation. This heightened expression of tumor suppressor and regulatory proteins can counteract oncogenic signals, such as those driven by eIF5A2, thereby inhibiting metastasis and angiogenesis and ultimately improving liver neoplasm prognosis. Our model will be rigorously tested using contemporary technologies including CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing, domain-specific mutants, single-molecule RNA FISH, co-immunoprecipitation/proximity labeling, and integrated multi-omics (transcriptomic and epitranscriptomic) profiling in both in vitro and in vivo liver cancer models.
CausalChain: Upregulation of CIAO2A -> Recruitment of mRNA export factors (NXF1, ALYREF) and RNA modification enzymes -> Enhanced deposition of RNA marks (e.g., m6A, pseudouridine) on tumor suppressor mRNAs (via recognition motifs) -> Selective and high-fidelity nuclear export of tumor suppressor transcripts -> Optimal expression of tumor suppressor/regulatory proteins -> Counteraction of oncogenic drivers (e.g., eIF5A2) -> Inhibition of metastasis and angiogenesis -> Improved liver neoplasm prognosis
